finding.claim: SQL injection via unvalidated ORDER BY: $_GET['sort'] is concatenated into the query. An attacker can use subqueries or CASE expressions for boolean/blind extraction of data from any table in the SQLite DB (e.g. sort=(CASE WHEN (SELECT substr(password,1,1) FROM users LIMIT 1)='a' THEN id ELSE name END)). Stacked queries are unlikely under SQLite PDO, but data exfiltration through ordering is feasible.

trace.note: concatenated directly into the ORDER BY clause of a query executed via PDO::query; column names cannot be parameterized and no allowlist is applied

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no auth check, no escaping in this function. The sibling list_users_safe (line 9-13) uses an allowlist, but list_users_sorted does not. Only one file exists in the codebase, so no upstream middleware could sanitize the input. Whether list_users_sorted is actually called is unknown, since no caller exists in this file.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 does concatenate $_GET['sort'] into ORDER BY with no allowlist or parameterization, so the sink is genuinely injectable. However, list.php only defines functions and never calls list_users_sorted, so I can't confirm it is reachable or whether the caller is authenticated, and the "unauthenticated" and `password` claims are unsupported.
